instruction: Right-align the heading in the document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent selected the heading text correctly, then clicked 'Align Right' instead of 'Align Center', resulting in right-aligned heading instead of centered. Final screenshot shows cursor moved into table.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in Writer, interact with alignment toolbar buttons, navigate document
metadata.failure_analysis: Model confused the right-align button with center-align. It selected the correct text but applied the wrong alignment (RIGHT instead of CENTER).
metadata.task_rationale: Since the model demonstrated it can right-align text (did so accidentally), this task asks it to do exactly what it already accomplished — right-align the heading.
metadata.explanation: Task asks to right-align the heading. Custom getter reads the DOCX first paragraph alignment. Metric checks if alignment is RIGHT.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads first paragraph alignment from the DOCX file using python-docx and maps alignment enum to string (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT/JUSTIFY)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_alignment') without wrapping in 'rules' key
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring up-to-date state
Expected value 'RIGHT' correctly matches the instruction requirement to right-align the heading
Single instruction requirement (right-align heading) is fully covered by the evaluator
Minor concern: getter assumes heading is doc.paragraphs[0]; if there are empty paragraphs before the heading, it could read the wrong paragraph
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making the getter more robust by finding the first non-empty paragraph or the first paragraph with a heading style, rather than always using paragraphs[0]
